title: Triage rotations prefill — weekly log 2026-06-21
body:
Triage rotations prefill — weekly log (2026-06-21 to 2026-06-23)

Context:
- Running a focused triage rota for prefill / KV cache regressions; goal is to reduce tail latency incidents and lower eviction churn during burst traffic. This doc captures daily standup notes, quick experiment outcomes, and follow-ups for the week.

Attendees (rotating): Elena, Marcus, Anya, Ravi, Tom (+ ad-hoc ESU from SRE).

Agenda:
- Quick incident recap from last week (p99 spike after kernel patch)
- Prefill & coalescing experiment status
- Shadow KV eviction metrics and tuning ideas
- Short-term mitigations for production traffic spikes
- Owners and tickets for next week

Notes / Observations: 
1) Kernel handshake patch (PR 1298) behavior:
- Patch reduced average generator CPU by ~8% on perf cluster but introduced a small p99 carryover when sequence lengths > 1.2k tokens.
- Reproducer: long-chat session + back-to-back streaming (see SRV-3412) — observed KV cache thrash when micro-batches aligned with seq-length boundary.

2) Prefill coalescing experiment (A/B):
- Setup: coalescer v2 enabled for 25% of traffic on us-west-int; target combining windows shortened from 12ms -> 6ms for suspected hot prefixes.
- Result summary: mean latency unchanged, tail (99.9) improved ~3.4% for chat workloads, but KV cache hit-rate dropped by 1.7% during burst windows. Hypothesis: smaller windows reduced useful prefetch grouping for long hist sessions.

3) KV cache eviction pattern:
- Observed increased churn in the 03:00–06:00 UTC window tied to nightly batch jobs from Dedicated customers; evictions spike correlated with temporary host reclaims during scaling.
- Temporary guardrail implemented: bump per-instance soft-reserve to 12% to reduce aggressive eviction during autoscale.

4) Batching heuristics:
- Microbatch aggregation timeout tweak: experiment to bias by request-size instead of time-of-arrival looks promising locally (reduction in pseudo-head-of-line blocking). Need perf harness run.

5) Incident followup:
- Rollback decision: kernel handshake patch was rolled back for prod us-west on 2026-06-20 after p99 regression post-deployment. Canary on staging kept.
- Action item to add synthetic long-seq + streaming test to pre-deploy suite (see action item below).

Action items:
- Elena: add synthetic long-seq + continuous streaming test to canary harness (ticket: SRV-3440) — due 2026-06-28.
- Marcus: run 24h perf sweep of coalescer v2 with varied window sizes (3ms, 6ms, 12ms) and produce CSV of p50/p95/p99/KV-hit — due 2026-06-25.
- Anya: instrument eviction telemetry with session-id tagging so we can tie evictions to customer autoscale events (PR draft in repo branch: eviction-telemetry) — due 2026-06-29.
- Ravi: prototype request-size-aware batching heuristic and benchmark against current heuristic on perf cluster (ticket: SRV-3442) — due 2026-07-02.
- Tom: coordinate with SRE to test soft-reserve bump during night jobs and measure eviction reduction (OpsPlaybook note) — due 2026-06-24.

Open questions / Risks:
- Does the kernel handshake optimization generalize across model families (decoder-only vs. encoder-decoder)? Need cross-model perf tests.
- Prefill coalescer smaller windows improved tail but reduced hit-rate in bursts — what tradeoff is acceptable for Dedicated vs Hosted customers? Consider routing policy by customer tier.
- Autoscale-driven host churn may continue to cause eviction spikes; long-term fix might require cache partitioning by customer or stronger session affinity.

Decisions made this week:
- Keep kernel patch gated in staging until long-seq streaming test added to canary.
- Continue coalescer v2 experiment on low-traffic canary cohorts and expand windows search space per Marcus's sweep.
- Implement short-term soft-reserve bump for instances during known nightly job windows.

Quick metrics snapshot (perf cluster / us-west-int, sampling window 2026-06-19 -> 2026-06-22):
- Baseline p50/p95/p99 before patch: 18ms / 42ms / 120ms
- After patch (staging): 17ms / 40ms / 134ms (p99 increased on very long seq traces)
- KV hit-rate baseline: 86.4% -> experiment 84.7% (during burst windows)
- Avg batch size: 3.1 tokens/request -> coalescer v2 cohort: 3.5

Reference links:
- Kernel handshake PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1298
- Incident ticket: SRV-3412
- Slack triage thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02SERVING/p1568387200

Notes to future readers:
- This doc is intentionally informal and intended for the triage rotation on-call. Add anything you tried and short results; keep commands and exact perf harness commands in GH runbooks rather than here.

Next sync: 2026-06-24, 9:30 PT (standup slot).
